Left-leaning U.S. surfers wobbly-knee’d and exhausted after shredding pumping “blue wave”

Beachgrit Home » Left-leaning U.S. surfers wobbly-knee’d and exhausted after shredding pumping “blue wave”

By Chas Smith

18 hours ago

Right-leaning U.S. surfers, meanwhile, blowing saltwater out of noses.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:43
Instaread

Left-leaning United States of American surfers woke up this morning with reddened eyes, sore shoulders, burning thighs and wobbly knees after a night spent shredding a much larger than expected blue wave. Yesterday was, of course, election day in the nation and polls were indicating that Democrats (colored blue) had a chance to flip both the House of Representatives and Senate. Dubiousness ran high, though, as those same polls have become unreliable in the past decade.

As early returns started coming in from the east coast, however, it became quickly clear that a blue wave was forming that could sweep across the plains breaking all the way in Alaska where two bros named Dan Sullivan were confusing each other.

Left-leaning surfers who had doubted the polls were forced to spend the night shredding the swell, which turned into a tsunami according to some news outlets, very much under-gunned, many on fishes or bonzers. Left-leaning surfers who had correctly predicted the conditions were dropping in on various rhino chasers, shouting over their shoulders “know before you go” to their foam lacking friends.

Right-leaning surfers, on the other hand, woke up this morning with severe post-nasal drip and busted ear drums after suffering a massive wipeout. Republicans lost bigly across the board with Florida governor “Meatball” Ron DeSantis predicting even more poundings come 2028 leading some right-leaning surfers to consider if a boogie board might be the better wave riding tool for the next few years.

Advertisement

But how did you spend last evening? Waxing and whacking or spitting sand out of your mouth?

Also, should we turn BeachGrit into a data center?

Wild times ahead.
